jobs.title: Mexico Claims Compliance, Performance & Operations Manager
jobs.description:
Claims Operations & Performance Manager

Who we are?

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.

We’re also committed to making a positive difference for our colleagues and in the communities where we work and live. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

Get to know the business !

General Insurance is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers. It includes one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. General Insurance offers a broad range of products to customers through a diversified, multichannel distribution network.

The Claims function is meant to be a partner to the business segments, offering support, expertise, and partnership. It is through a proper and market leading claims service that all business efforts materialize the continuity of client and broker relationships in the long term. The existing diversity of the business portfolio demands from the claims role specialized expertise in the different business areas. The claims managers heading each line of business work partner with Underwriters and other key stakeholders to support a wide array of products and offerings, through a complex and highly demanding distribution force and network. Claims has the responsibility of delivering and materializing the product offer and promise. A policy is a promise and the handling and resolution of a claim is the moment to fulfill that promise and make a significant difference.

The Claims Operations and Performance Manager supports the head of claims by properly managing the following functions that are designed to monitor the Claims operation, to provide quantitative feedback and to support the development of evalution and development of solutions in an iterative and ongoing cycle of continuous improvement of the Claims operation:

- Compliance : ensuring that the control environment meets the high standards established by the various regulations that govern the Claims role. These various regulations pertain to a wide array of control frameworks ranging from internal best practice guidelines to regulatory requirements.  Properly managing and enhancing this control framework is the basis for empowering the various claims teams.
- Vendor Management : Both local regulation, and internal guidelines establish that all Claims vendors must have a contract. Some of these contracts are subject to a very specific local regulation (REPSE) and require intensive follow up in terms of requirements that must be met. Compliance with this requirement determines whether the usage of such vendors can be registered as tax deductible.
- First notice of loss (FNOL): properly managing this activity which creates capacity within the technical handling teams by absorbing this activity (which is of a low variability in nature) and seeks to find solutions for efficiency and automation.
- Business Analytics: properly managing the exploitation of data to the benefit of better assessing the efficiency of the operation and allowing for better decisions by claims management. Ensuring that the flow of data is adequate by ensuring that adequacy of the source of data.
- Process evaluation and Continuous Improvement : proper assessment of the “as is” status of the operation will eventually lead to determining the correct “target” KPI´s, processes and controls. This analysis will imply the need for improvement projects and initiatives that need to be led and pushed by claims management through the support of this role.

About the role

What you need to know:
- Deep understanding of the insurance industry and the claims process. Understanding of the context and roles of each of the main types of claims vendors (i.e. adjusters, lawyers, consultants, salvage companies, recovery agents, etc.).
- Basic understanding of the claims function and how it relates to the different areas of an insurance company (i.e. UW, operations, audit, sales, etc.)
- Design, understand, and map complex processes; manage apps/tools to present quickly and efficiently these to internal and external stakeholders.
- Good practices to map, manage and audit risks inherent to the documented processes of the claims department.
- Design, understand and create underlying policies and procedures; manage process to accurately describe operational realities into documented policies and procedures.
- Management, enhancement, maintenance, and training of all aspects of the anti-money laundry framework.
- Best practices related to security information and data protection activities.
- Good vendor management practices and local regulatory requirements.
- Quality statistical control tools and principles.
- Industrial Engineering principles in terms of Continuous Improvement, Total Quality Control, Lean Processes, Kaizen, etc.
- Data management software (i.e. Excel) and business intelligence solutions (i.e. Power BI)

How does this knowledge translate into action?
- Partnering with line managers and handlers to map operational processes to assess these from a compliance and risk management perspective. This is a continuous monitoring key in a constantly evolving context (fiscal, regulatory, etc.).
- Once mapped, conduct ongoing preventive assessments, reviews, and analysis to provide constructive feedback to line managers which will ensure a robust operation is in place.
- Being an in-house claims resource with market information regarding key compliance topics like anti-money laundry guidelines, to assess for example how to onboard new complex accounts.
- Supporting the Head of Claims to comply with internal and external local regulation to ensure that a pool of +500 suppliers meet international standards as well as local regulation. Ensure that an appropriate evaluation of the performance of key vendors is effective and timely.
- Effectively managing individuals that perform manual data entries into the claims system (FNOL) in a cost-effective manner and with the appropriate data quality. Ensuring that the usage of human resources is effectively combined with the usage of automation and RPA technology.
- Understand the data structure and system platform. Develop plans to provide analytics to the different stakeholders of the insurance company (within and outside of Claims). Develop plans and solutions to guarantee the accuracy and consistency of the data provided to evaluate the operation and develop action plans.
- Design and lead data driven solutions to address operational problems and deficiencies related to process, human and/or systemic nature. Align these evaluations with the overall value-added initiative of the company. Provide insights and information to management that can be taken to market and allow for AIG to differentiate from its competitors in the insurance market.

What we’re looking for:
- Academic background: Industrial Engineering, Finance, Accounting or Business administration.
- Experience: - +5 years in Operations, Process, Auditing and/or Quality Control activities in banking, insurance, or financial service industries.
- Specialization or experience in Audit related positions is a plus.
- Understanding and/or participation in compliance activities (i.e. Solvency II, governance committees, etc.) is a plus.
- Experience in quality control projects is a plus.
- Exposure to continuous improvement projects like statistical quality control projects or system implementation initiatives.
- Process mapping.
- Management of Excel, Power BI, etc.

- Key soft skills of the position: balance between high and stringent controls and ever evolving needs of operational reality.
- Incumbent needs to be a team player that needs to be recognized in the team as effective partner.
- Other key skills are good communication, powerful synthesis, situational leadership.

At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike.

Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters
At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.

Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world
American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. At AIG, you can go further to support individuals, businesses, and communities, helping them to manage risk, respond to times of uncertainty and discover new potential. jobs.description:
At Talbot and AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as our Head of Operations to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Talbot
Talbot operates within the Lloyd's Insurance Market through Syndicate 1183, Syndicate 2019, Syndicate 2478 and Syndicate 2479.
Part of AIG since 2018, Talbot is committed to working with brokers and clients to deliver industry leading solutions. It is headquartered in London with offices in New York and Singapore with more than 350 employees.
With an expert team of highly skilled and experienced underwriters and a balanced, geographically diverse portfolio of business, Talbot has earned a reputation as an industry leading insurance and reinsurance specialist.
Talbot writes a diversified portfolio including Crisis Management, Energy, Financial Lines, Marine, Political Risk, Property, Transport and Terrorism.  Drawing on our deep industry expertise, Talbot develops tailored insurance solutions that address clients' evolving and often unique needs.

How you will create an impact

Responsibilities:

- Create and drive Operations’ strategy supporting Talbot’s strategy. Deliver agreed business targets, operational plans and change priorities in partnership with internal and external parties.
- Partner with business leaders to understand customer and operational needs and translate these into service, process and control requirements.
- Represent Talbot at various LMA forums.
- Design and embed the most effective operating model, utilising third parties where appropriate, ensuring cost efficiency and service standards are met.
- Own Outsource Service Provider (OSP) relationships: onboard new providers, manage and monitor performance, and exit services when required; ensure delivery aligns with operating standards, policies and controls.
- Support CFO in oversight of procurement and vendor management, and work with Global Sourcing & Procurement Services to ensure processes work effectively.

Governance and Controls
- Ensure all regulatory, legislative and operational standards and codes of practice are met, including Lloyd’s expectations and standards where applicable, with effective checks, balances, monitoring and controls.
- Ensure the operating model supports Lloyd’s oversight and reporting needs, including timely provision of operational MI and evidence for internal governance, audit activity and Lloyd’s/prudential reviews.
- Own and be accountable for operational risks, standards and policy implementation, ensuring mitigations and controls are in place.
- Continuously monitor, review and identify areas for improvement and processes to establish effective of controls.
- Support internal and external audit where necessary.

Management and Leadership
- Manage capacity, cost and resources to deliver service to budget in support of country and regional plans.
- Build, lead and develop an Operations team to continuously improve performance while maintaining agreed standards and controls.
- Identify training and coaching needs for direct reports, driving capability development and providing performance feedback in line with HR processes.
- Motivate, coach and develop future leaders through development plans, talent management and succession planning

.

- Detailed knowledge of operational excellence tools and techniques
- Extensive knowledge of underwriting processes such that the relationship between Operations, Underwriting, Claims and other functions is seamless.
- Extensive experience in the insurance industry, specifically Lloyd’s/ London Market (re)insurance, with an excellent knowledge of the Lloyd’s Market, its regulatory requirements.
- In-depth experience in managing a Team
- Experience of devising, organizing and implementing large scale, complex projects, incorporating multiple work streams and multiple stakeholders
- Experience of strategic planning and working with the Executives to drive the Operations agenda across the business

- Ability to interpret market and macros trends, understand how this impacts on the business operations and identify strategies that will support the business competitiveness.
- Analytical skills and understanding to deliver focused growth and profitable business outcomes Leadership
- Ability to negotiate with major stakeholders, balancing execution requirements and business needs
- Ability to negotiate with major stakeholders, balancing execution requirements and business needs
- Ability to self-manage but awareness of when its necessary to involve senior managers on key issues

New York, Boston, Chicago, Atlanta, Washington DC, Miami, Dallas, Houston, Denver, San Francisco, Los Angeles

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. AIG member companies provide a wide range of property casualty insurance in approximately 70 countries and jurisdictions. These diverse offerings include products and services that help businesses and individuals protect their assets and manage risks.

We’re also committed to making a positive difference for our colleagues and in the communities where we work and live. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

About the Business
AIG Underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, and Multinational Clients. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

About the Role
This key leadership role focuses on technical underwriting of complex and sophisticated insurable risks as they relate to Representations and Warranties transactions (including analysis of deal documents and due diligence) and development of relationships with M&A source producers (brokers, lawyers, private equity fund principals, and corporate professionals).

The Underwriting Leader will be responsible for the structuring, underwriting and negotiation of transactional insurance solutions, with a principal focus on representations and warranties insurance, and will provide leadership and technical guidance throughout the underwriting process, and contribute to the formulation and implementation of the Group’s strategy at the product line level, including underwriting appetite, portfolio quality, broker engagement and profitable growth initiatives.

Responsibilities

- Conduct background research on the parties to a particular transaction and the industries in which they operate.
- Review and understand the client's motivation for requesting the insurance coverage, the role the insurance is playing in the transaction, and the value of the insurance to the transaction.
- Review and understand the agreements and other documentation relevant to the analysis and assessment of the risk.
- Analyze and assess complex and highly negotiated risks in accordance with the relevant product line policies and procedures, exercising sound judgment on coverage, structure, pricing and risk selection.
- Prepare and negotiate non-binding indication letters, insurance policies and binder agreements.
- Serve as a key point of contact for clients, clients’ advisors, brokers and other deal professionals, providing clear, commercially focused guidance throughout the underwriting process.
- Lead and participate in underwriting conference calls.
- Manage the underwriting process and the selection of and work performed by outside counsel and other advisors.
- Present preliminary findings and conclusions to management.
- Provide technical guidance, coaching and support to less experienced underwriters, analysts, and other team members and contribute to consistent underwriting practices across the Group.
- The Underwriting Leader will play a meaningful role in the execution of the Group’s relationship development and marketing plan: - Participate in the marketing of transactional insurance products to brokers, private equity firms, law firms, investment banks, accounting firms, consulting firms and prospective clients, with a focus on strengthening strategic relationships and identifying new business opportunities.
- Develop and deliver sophisticated presentation, marketing and informational materials tailored to clients, brokers and other M&A professionals.
- Help develop, refine and enhance the suite of transactional insurance products offered to our clients based on market developments, claims experience and evolving transaction structures.

Leadership Skills
- Exceptional written and oral communication skills, including advanced proficiency in drafting clear, precise legal and commercial documents;
- Advanced understanding of complex corporate structuring and financing arrangements;
- Demonstrated ability to lead negotiations with commercially and legally sophisticated advisors, brokers and clients;
- Highly focused, enthusiastic and creative thinker with strong judgment and a solutions-oriented approach to novel or complex issues;
- Demonstrated ability to lead and manage multiple complex underwriting processes, assess and prioritize material risks, coordinate stakeholders and maintain organization under demanding transaction timelines;
- Strong interpersonal and leadership skills, with a demonstrated ability to collaborate effectively across functions, geographies and levels of seniority;
- Proven ability to make sound commercial decisions against a backdrop of complex legal, financial and underwriting risk assessment; and
- Ability to operate with a high degree of independence, initiative, accountability and professional judgment.

Technical Skills and Experience
- Advanced competency in understanding complex corporate M&A transactions and drafting transaction documents;
- Advanced negotiating and relationship-management skills, including the ability to influence outcomes and resolve complex issues;
- Deep knowledge of transactional legal exposures (warranty breaches, tax structuring issues, litigation and the computation and measure of damages);
- Strong financial and commercial acumen, including the ability to analyze financial statements, financial reports, quality of earnings reports and other commercial due diligence materials;
- Demonstrated ability to prepare and deliver compelling presentations to brokers, regional offices, legal advisors, clients and other sophisticated audiences;
- At least 7 years of professional experience in M&A legal, underwriting, corporate finance or another relevant business discipline, including at least 3 years of direct underwriting experience with M&A insurance products; and
- Significant experience with insurance sector or other financial institutions, including a strong understanding of underwriting discipline, portfolio considerations and the M&A insurance marketplace.

jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
At Talbot and AIG, we are reimagining the way we help customers to manage risk. Join us as our Chief of Staff to play your part in that transformation. It’s an opportunity to grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

Make your mark in Talbot
Talbot operates within the Lloyd's Insurance Market through Syndicate 1183, Syndicate 2019, Syndicate 2478 and Syndicate 2479.
Part of AIG since 2018, Talbot is committed to working with brokers and clients to deliver industry leading solutions. It is headquartered in London with offices in New York and Singapore with more than 350 employees.
With an expert team of highly skilled and experienced underwriters and a balanced, geographically diverse portfolio of business, Talbot has earned a reputation as an industry leading insurance and reinsurance specialist.
Talbot writes a diversified portfolio including Crisis Management, Energy, Financial Lines, Marine, Political Risk, Property, Transport and Terrorism.  Drawing on our deep industry expertise, Talbot develops tailored insurance solutions that address clients' evolving and often unique needs.

How you will create an impact
The Chief of Staff (CoS) will act as a strategic partner to the CEO, helping translate Talbot’s goals and objectives into focused execution, enabling the successful delivery of strategic, financial, operational and people plans. The role operates across Talbot and AIG to drive alignment, accelerate key priorities, improve leadership effectiveness and ensure the CEO and leadership team are focused on the decisions and initiatives that will have the greatest impact

They will be instrumental in enabling Talbot to deliver its business objectives across the AIG Group, effectively managing relationships with other stakeholders. They will also act in an advisory capacity to the CEO in matters relating to business management and leadership, strategy, communications, people management and financial planning. They will be providing thought leadership, generating ideas and driving initiatives to improve business performance and providing meaningful contributions towards resolution of day-to-day and ongoing management issues.

The position demands a high level of initiative and autonomy to add value, enable business growth, to take corrective action and institute new processes, projects and activities. With strong relationships across AIG, within the Lloyd’s corporation and across the Lloyd’s market, the CoS will influence outcomes at a strategic level.

Key Accountabilities/Responsibilities

CEO Leverage & Priorities
- Act as a trusted thought partner and sounding board to the CEO.  As a confidante, discussion partner and advisor to the CEO, this role will providing thought leadership; supporting creation of ideas and resolution of issues
- Translate the CEO’s vision into clear priorities, decisions and actions.
- Anticipate needs, identify risks and develop solutions for the CEO to consider
- Responsible for preparing and briefing the CEO prior to external meetings and/or events including; drafting talking points, speeches, briefing notes or analysis.

Strategic Execution
- Strategic Execution; turn strategic priorities into executable plans with clear owners, milestones and outcomes (leveraging project & programme management experience)
- Identify blockers and drive resolution across the business.
- Directly assist the CEO in all day to day operations, including a variety of complex tasks and ensure the activities are aligned to business goals and priorities. Streamlining these activities and helping to ensure the highest quality of delivery
- Identify and drive opportunities for change across the business.

Leadership team effectiveness & organisational influence
- Prepare the CEO and Leadership team for key meetings and decisions
- Establish strong meeting rhythms, agendas and follow-up.
- Support the CEO in managing the Leadership team’s effectiveness and dynamics
- Ensure decisions are clearly communicated and acted upon
- Plan, coordinate and lead meetings, prepare information, monitor status of action items.
- Ensure leaders understand and remain focused on the most critical areas; challenges competing priorities and help to resolve where functions are pulling in different directions.
- Bring the right leaders together to resolve cross-functional issues; surfacing disagreements and competing perspectives.
- Structure discussions so the leadership team moves from debate to decision.

Communication & Stakeholder management
- Act as an extension of the CEO when appropriate; credibly presenting to the leadership team or senior stakeholders as necessary.

- Draft or shape key communications, presentations and Leadership materials ensure consistent messaging around priorities and values.
- Manage relationships with senior stakeholders, partners or the Board where relevant.
- Maintain interdepartmental working relationships; identify priorities and organize daily assignments.
- Takes a lead in organizing/setting the agenda for corporate events and strategy off-sites as directed by the CEO and in collaboration with their Executive Assistant.

Business Planning Insight & Analysis
- Research, compile, analyse and summarize data for special projects and/or reports; developing recommendations on strategic and operational matters as required
- Anticipate, prioritize, and interpret business or operational challenges that may impede on the business objectives and recommend actions to address.
- Liaise with other departments on issues needing the  CEO’s feedback/recommendation and develop strong relationships across Talbot and AIG.

jobs.description:
Join us as a Senior Underwriter, Representations and Warranties - M&A Financial Lines to play a highly influential role in protecting our clients and growing our business.

Make your mark in Underwritin g
AIG Underwriting teams help to find insurance solutions in areas including Financial Lines, Property, Casualty, Specialty Lines, Cyber, and Multinational Clients. We are reimagining how we help customers to manage risk, transforming our operating model and reshaping our role responsibilities and career pathways. The goal is to unlock the full potential in each colleague – empowering our people to grow as insurance professionals and add more value to our customers and AIG.

How you will create an impac t

This key role focuses on technical underwriting of insurable risks as they relate to Representations and Warranties transactions (including analysis of deal documents and due diligence) and development of relationships with M&A source producers (brokers, lawyers, private equity fund principals, and corporate professionals). The Senior Underwriter will be responsible for the structuring, underwriting and negotiation of transactional insurance solutions, with a principal focus on representations and warranties insurance.

Among other things, the Senior Underwriter will:

- Conduct background research on the parties to a particular transaction and the industries in which they operate.
- Review and understand the client's motivation for requesting the insurance coverage, the role the insurance is playing in the transaction, and the value of the insurance to the transaction.
- Review and understand the agreements and other documentation relevant to the analysis and assessment of the risk.
- Analyze and assess the underlying risk in accordance with the relevant product line policies and procedures.
- Prepare and negotiate non-binding indication letters, insurance policies and binder agreements.
- Interact with clients, client’s advisors, brokers and other deal professionals.
- Lead and participate on underwriting conference calls.
- Manage the underwriting process and the  selection of and work performed by outside counsel and other advisors.
- Present preliminary findings and conclusions to management.
- The Senior Underwriter will participate in the execution of the Group’s relationship development and marketing plan. Among other things, the Senior Underwriter will:  - Participate in the marketing of transactional insurance products to brokers, private equity firms, law firms, investment banks, accounting firms, consulting firms, and prospective clients.
- Develop and prepare presentation, marketing and informational materials.
- Continue to develop and refine the suite of transactional insurance products offered to our clients.
- Participate in the formulation and implementation of the Group's strategy at the product line level.

What you will need to succeed

LEADERSHIP SKILLS:
- Strong written and oral communication skills; extremely proficient in drafting of legal and commercial documents;
- Detailed understanding of complex corporate structuring and financing arrangements;
- Ability to negotiate with commercially and legally sophisticated advisors, brokers and clients;
- Highly focused, enthusiastic and creative thinker;
- Ability to manage a complex underwriting process, assess risk and stay organized;
- Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaboratively work on a global basis;
- Ability to understand and execute commercial decision making against a backdrop of legal risk assessment; and
- Ability to be a self-starter and work independently.

TECHNICAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE:
- High competency in understanding complex corporate M&A transactions and drafting transaction documents;
- Strong negotiating skills;
- Specific knowledge of transactional legal exposures (warranty breaches, tax structuring issues, litigation and computation and measure of damages);
- General knowledge of and ability to comprehend financial statements, financial reports,  quality of earnings reports and other commercial due diligence materials;
- Competency in preparing and giving presentations to brokers, regional offices, legal advisors, clients and others;
- 5 or more years’ experience in M&A legal, underwriting, corporate finance or another relevant business; and
- Specific experience with insurance sector or other financial institutions a strong plus.

Ready to step up to new challenges? We would love to hear from you.

The base salary range for this position is $220,000-$250,000, and the position is eligible for a bonus in accordance with the terms of the applicable incentive plan. If your compensation expectations are above the posted range, we still encourage you to apply - your unique background matters to us. We’re proud to offer a range of competitive benefits, a summary of which can be viewed here: US Benefits Overview .

jobs.description:
General Manager Austria and Switzerland

Location: Zurich/Switzerland

At AIG, we are reimagining how we help customers manage risk. Join us as  General Manager ACH (Austria and Switzerland)  and play a key role in that transformation. This is an opportunity to grow your leadership impact as a valued member of the team.

Who we are:
American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a leading global insurance organization. Building on more than 100 years of experience, AIG member companies provide a wide range of property-casualty insurance, life insurance, retirement solutions, and other financial services to customers in over 80 countries and jurisdictions. These offerings help businesses and individuals protect their assets, manage risk, and plan for retirement security.

Get to know the business:
General Insurance is a leading provider of insurance products and services for commercial and personal insurance customers. It includes one of the world’s most extensive property-casualty networks and delivers a broad product portfolio through a diversified, multi-channel distribution model.

About the role

The  General Manager Austria and Switzerland (ACH)  is responsible for leading operations in Switzerland and Austria. The role is part of the DACH (Germany, Austria, and Switzerland) Senior Leadership Team and reports to the General Manager DACH.

As  AIG’s General Manager, , ACH you will drive strategic initiatives, oversee operations, and hold full P&L responsibility, supporting business performance across both countries through your leadership team.

Business Management
- Lead the Austrian and Swiss branches with full accountability for underwriting discipline, portfolio quality, and sustainable growth.
- Own the Austrian and Swiss P&L, including delivery against profitability and growth targets.
- Develop and execute country business strategies (within AIG GI International parameters) and annual financial plans for both markets.
- Steer distribution performance across channels, with particular focus on strategic broker partnerships, retention, and new production.
- Ensure high-performing operations across Underwriting, Claims, Distribution, and all support functions.
- Monitor, report, and proactively address operational risks, opportunities, and development plans against agreed company objectives.
- Drive continuous operational improvement initiatives with clear impact on service quality, efficiency, and cost discipline.
- Ensure robust governance, systems, controls, and full regulatory compliance across both country organizations, including effective local regulatory engagement.

External Relationship Management
- Represent AIG with major clients and broker partners to strengthen market position and accelerate profitable growth.
- Expand and elevate the AIG (DACH) brand and external profile across both markets.
- Build, manage, and sustain effective relationships with regulators and key external stakeholders, including escalation and issue-resolution leadership when required.

People Management
- Lead hiring and resource allocation decisions in line with regional and global governance structures.
- Build and sustain a diverse, inclusive, and high-performance culture across both countries.
- Drive talent identification, succession planning, and leadership development to ensure a strong pipeline of future leaders.
- Set clear performance expectations, coach leaders, and hold teams accountable for results and behaviors.
- Communicate the AIG DACH vision, mission, and strategic direction of AIG GI International with clarity and consistency.
- Serve as an active member of the DACH Senior Leadership Team.

What we’re looking for:

Leadership Skills:
- Proven record of financial and operational success in general insurance, delivering profitable growth and leading effectively through change.
- Strong executive client presence, with the ability to represent AIG credibly and build long-term strategic relationships in both markets.
- Experienced people leader and organization builder with a strong focus on developing talent and leadership capability.
- Demonstrated ability to attract, retain, and develop high-caliber talent and build diverse, high-performing teams.
- Proven ability to influence and align a broad set of internal and external stakeholders.
- Highly collaborative leadership style across functions, countries, and geographies.
- Strong ability to lead and influence within complex matrix structures and cross-border environments.

Technical Skills and Expertise:
- Significant industry experience, market credibility, and recognized expertise in one or more insurance product lines.
- Several years of experience leading country operations or large functional/product teams within the DACH region.
- Strategic and results-oriented leader who translates bold vision into actionable plans and measurable business outcomes.
- Ability to represent AIG persuasively in internal and external forums, including client and broker meetings and industry events.
- Proven track record of operating successfully within an international insurance carrier and navigating cross-border complexity.
- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with fluency in written and spoken German and English.

Core Competencies:
- Drive for profitable results
- Strategic leadership
- Collaboration and influence
- Execution in a matrix structure
- Talent development
